prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

S021: Marine coordination covers the Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, and applicable vessel operating procedures.
S022: Workforce interfaces include access management through the North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, and Personnel Tracking Console.
S023: Supply interfaces cover inventory and replenishment coordination through the Warehouse System and Spares Hub.
S024: External interfaces include weather services, metocean observations, grid dispatch, port support, and emergency response organizations.
S025: Cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, and backup power are treated as enabling functions within the farm operations boundary.
S026: This section establishes the operating context and naming convention for the offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system.
S027: The system boundary covers offshore generation assets, supporting marine and shore facilities, operational personnel, and external organizations involved in farm activities.
S028: The farm operates in a variable marine environment where access, equipment condition, and grid requirements influence the timing and conduct of work.
S029: Canonical entity names are used throughout this document to identify system parts, actors, operational states, and controlled items.
S030: In this document, Turbine Controller is referred to by the alias Glassfin.
S031: In this document, Offshore Substation is referred to by the alias Morrowick.
S032: In this document, Weather Service is referred to by the alias Pale Lantern.
S033: The Turbine Controller represents the control function associated with an individual turbine.
S034: Pitch System and Rotor Brake Unit are turbine subsystems considered within the operational boundary.
S035: Converter Cabinet and Nacelle Condition Monitor are treated as distinct turbine equipment for maintenance planning and condition review.
S036: The Blade Inspection Drone is an operational asset used for turbine blade assessment.
S037: The Offshore Substation provides the farm's offshore electrical collection and switching environment.
S038: Main Transformer and Export Cable Monitor are included as substation and export-system assets, respectively.
S039: SCADA Gateway is the supervisory interface associated with farm monitoring and control operations.
S040: Shore Control Room provides a shore-based operating location for authorized personnel.
S041: Fleet Dispatch Console supports the coordination of operational resources across the farm.
S042: Maintenance Planning Engine supports the preparation and sequencing of maintenance activities.
S043: Weather Service represents the external weather information capability considered by farm operations.
S044: Metocean Buoy represents an offshore source of environmental observations within the operating context.
